name: P3-practo
prompt: Below are 6 numbered screenshots of the Practo mobile app (Android) captured by the owner as a DESIGN REFERENCE (call them P1..P6 in the order provided). For EACH screenshot: (1) identify the screen (home, search, doctor listing, doctor profile, clinic/hospital page, booking flow, filters, orders, chat, health hub, account, etc.), (2) describe its visual design in depth: layout structure, list/card design, PHOTO usage (are doctor/clinic photos shown? circular avatars? sizes?), typography hierarchy (sizes/weights), the color system (what reads as primary vs secondary/accent color; approximate hex), components (chips, badges, pills, tabs, bottom nav, ratings, buttons, banners), spacing/density feel, (3) name the ONE design element that most makes this screen feel premium/desirable. This informs a redesign of another Indian healthcare booking app, so extract transferable patterns. Be concrete and honest.
verdict:
# Practo Reference Screens — Detailed Breakdown

## P1 — Specialities Directory ("Find Doctors", part 1)

**Screen type:** Speciality taxonomy/index page for in-clinic doctor discovery.

**Visual design:**
- **Layout:** Solid indigo app bar (#2E3192-ish) with back arrow, "Find Doctors" title (white, bold, ~20sp), city selector "Bangalore ⌄" right-aligned — location context always visible. Below: white body, single-column scroll, 4-column icon grid with generous vertical spacing (~150px row height). Dense but breathing.
- **List/card design:** No cards — flat white background, each cell is a circular illustrated icon (~110px) over a soft lavender/blue gradient disc (#D9DCF5 → #E8EAF9), label below in 2–3 lines, centered.
- **Photo usage:** Zero photography. Custom flat illustrations (coral #F2836B, purple #5C4B9E, skin-tone orange) — humanized, anatomical, friendly.
- **Typography:** Single hierarchy level for labels: ~18sp regular-weight dark grey (#3A3A3A), centered, wraps to 2–3 lines. Section header "All specialities" ~26sp semi-bold. Long names ellipsize ("Diabetes Managem…").
- **Color system:** Primary = deep indigo/navy (#2B2D8F). Secondary accent = coral/salmon (#F2836B) inside illustrations. Tertiary = lavender gradient discs. White surfaces.
- **Components:** Just app bar + grid + section title. Minimal chrome; bottom gesture bar only.
- **Spacing feel:** Airy, icon-led, scannable; no cards or shadows = quiet, catalog-like.

**Premium element:** The consistent illustrated circular icon system — a bespoke illustration language across ~25 specialities reads as invested/owned, vs generic clip-art.

---

## P2 — Specialities Directory (part 2, scrolled tail)

**Screen type:** Same page scrolled to the end (Ayurveda → Cancer → Urinary → Veterinary → Diet & Nutrition).

**Visual design:**
- Identical system: indigo app bar persists (nice sticky context), 4-col grid, gradient discs, coral/purple illustrations.
- Content breadth is the story — ends with Veterinary and Diet & Nutrition, signaling "everything on one app."
- One label typo ("Digesitve Issues") — honest note: grid wrapping causes awkward breaks ("Homeopath y", "Physiothera py"), a real weakness of forcing long names into fixed 4 columns.

**Premium element:** Exhaustive, consistent taxonomy — a complete illustrated catalog with zero visual drift from first icon to last signals production quality.

---

## P3 — Consult a Doctor (online consult hub)

**Screen type:** Online consultation landing page (top: promos + search + top specialities).

**Visual design:**
- **Layout:** Same indigo app bar with "HELP" text button on the right. Body: (1) horizontal carousel of promo banners (~75% width card + peek of next card, 3-dot page indicator with active dark-blue dot), (2) "Search Health Problem / Symptoms" section header + pill search bar (light grey #F1F2F7 fill, rounded ~28px, grey magnifier + example-driven placeholder "Eg: Cold, cough, fever"), (3) "CHOOSE FROM TOP SPECIALITIES" 4-col icon grid with a special "VIEW ALL" circle (white, thin outline, teal uppercase text) as the 8th cell, (4) "Common Health Issues" grid begins.
- **Photo usage:** None — illustrations only; the banner is a rich designed graphic (purple Diwali theme, gold "SAVE 10%", diya illustrations, pill-shaped coupon-code chip "Use code: DIWALI10").
- **Typography:** Section headers ~24–26sp bold dark-grey; grid labels ~17sp regular. Mixed case headers here ("Search Health…") vs uppercase eyebrow ("CHOOSE FROM TOP SPECIALITIES") — slight inconsistency.
- **Color:** Primary indigo #2B2D8F; banner purple #4A2A8C with gold #E8A930; teal (#1BA9C4-ish) for VIEW ALL link; grey fill inputs.
- **Spacing:** Comfortable; sections separated by ~48px; carousel peeks to imply scrollability.

**Premium element:** The example-rich search placeholder + promo carousel pairing — it teaches the user what to type while feeling merchandised, like a consumer product rather than a medical tool.

---

## P4 — Consult a Doctor (Common Health Issues + GP/Ortho symptom grids)

**Screen type:** Same consult hub, scrolled — symptom browsing by speciality.

**Visual design:**
- Section pattern locked in: bold ~26sp header ("General Physician", "Orthopedist") → 4-col circular illustration grid → next section. Repetition creates rhythm.
- Illustrations now show *conditions*, not organs (Thyroid, Fungal Infection magnified-skin, Back Pain figure) — matching symptom-search intent.
- Same color trio (indigo/coral/lavender), same label typography, consistent disc gradients.
- Density: headers get more whitespace above than below — correct optical grouping.

**Premium element:** Symptom-first IA — users browse by "Back Pain," not by medical jargon; the illustrations carry the entire information load.

---

## P5 — Consult a Doctor (Dermatology/ENT/Gynae sections)

**Screen type:** Same page, deeper scroll.

**Visual design:**
- Confirms the pattern scales: 4 sections per viewport, identical grid cells. "Ear-Nose-Throat (ENT) Specialist" shows full clinical naming vs shorthand elsewhere.
- Two illustration styles drift slightly (Sore Throat on white vs gradient discs; acne-style portraits vs organ diagrams) — minor inconsistency, honest observation.
- Labels wrap awkwardly again ("Menopaus e", "Constinati…") — the 4-col grid is too tight for medical vocabulary.

**Premium element:** Sheer depth with visual discipline — hundreds of conditions navigable without lists or text walls; the grid is the entire UI.

---

## P6 — Consult a Doctor (Urologist/Sexologist/Psychiatry/Diabetology)

**Screen type:** Same page, sensitive-category section.

**Visual design:**
- Notable: Urologist section has only 2 items, centered as a 2-col row — the grid flexes to content, avoiding empty cells.
- Sensitive conditions (HIV, Erectile Problems, Premature Ejaculation) are handled with the same neutral, clinical-cute illustration treatment as fever — no red-flag styling, no shame aesthetic. This is a deliberate, transferable content-design decision.
- Typography/color identical throughout; "Schizophre nia" wrap issue again.

**Premium element:** Destigmatized, uniform visual treatment of sensitive health topics — the design communicates judgment-free care.

---

# Transferable patterns for a redesign

1. **Deep indigo (#2B2D8F) as a confident, single primary** across every app bar — with white text, one right-side utility action (city / HELP). Consistency > variety.
2. **Illustrated circular icon system** as the identity layer instead of stock photos: 4-column gradient-disc grid, one bespoke illustration set for specialities *and* symptoms. This is the app's biggest asset.
3. **Symptom-first IA:** let users enter by "Acne / Back Pain / Fever," grouped under plain-language speciality headers, with a search bar seeded with examples ("Eg: Cold, cough, fever").
4. **Grid that flexes** (2-item row centered) + "VIEW ALL" outline-circle as a grid cell.
5. **Persistent location context** in the header for clinic flows.
6. **Carousel with peek + page dots** for promos; coupon code as a pill chip inside the banner.
7. **Fix if copying:** 4 columns break long medical words — go 3 columns or auto-size labels; enforce one illustration style and one header case style.
